claim: Target Corporation is the name of the business that owner of the George D. Dayton House founded. It was later expanded by the Dutch founder of bookstore B. Dalton.
evidencia:
Page: Bruce Dayton. Sentence: Dayton was the last surviving of member of the five Dayton brothers – all grandsons of George Dayton, the founder of The Dayton Company – who expanded their grandfather's Dayton's department store in downtown Minneapolis from a single location into the national Target Corporation, one of the largest retail store chains in the United States.
Page: Bruce Dayton. Sentence: Dayton served as the chief executive officer (CEO) of the Dayton Hudson Corporation, the company now known as the Target Corporation, before becoming the chairman of Dayton Hudson from 1970 to 1977.
Page: George Dayton. Sentence: George Draper Dayton (March 6, 1857 – February 18, 1938) was an American businessman and philanthropist, most famous for being the founder of Dayton's department store, which later became Target Corporation.
Page: B. Dalton. Sentence: B. Dalton Bookseller (often called B. Dalton or B. Dalton's) was an American retail bookstore chain founded in 1966 by Bruce Dayton, a member of the same family that operated the Dayton's department store chain.
Page: George D. Dayton House. Sentence: George Dayton hired the Sioux Falls architect Wallace L. Dow to design his grand home on a parcel that took up eight lots.

- Bruce Dayton served as chief executive officer of Dayton Hudson Corporation, the company now known as Target Corporation.
- Bruce Dayton became chairman of Dayton Hudson Corporation and served in that role from 1970 to 1977.
- Bruce Dayton was the last surviving member of the five Dayton brothers.
